reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Ishmaelite, Midianite, and Medanite as interchangeable names for one Abrahamic trading band that outsiders often confused.

discrepancy.note: Colenso reads Genesis 37 as fusing two independent accounts, one crediting Midianite kidnappers and the other an Ishmaelite caravan.

quotes.text: In E (xxxvii.28»,36), certain Midianites appear to have kidnapped Joseph, and sold him into Egypt: in X (xxxvii.25-27,28''), his brothers sell him to a caravan of IshmaclUes, and they bring him down to Egj'pt, and sell him there, xxxix.l.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), ch. VI, on Genesis 37:28 and Genesis 37:36.

sides.snippet: sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. They brought Joseph into Egypt.
sides.verseText: Midianites who were merchants passed by, and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. They brought Joseph into Egypt.

sides.snippet: The Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh's, the captain of the guard.
